## Automated Tests Required

### vox-010 — Region-file format + paged residency working set — Integration
**Test file path**: `neues-spiel/tests/integration/voxel_world/region_file_residency_test.gd`
(or a documented playtest, per the story's own declared alternate)

**What to test** (from story AC-1/2/3 / `TR-voxel-world-053/041/021`):
- Resident-set membership: given a world larger than one region, an injected camera focus point,
  and a settlement region, the resident set contains **exactly** camera-near ∪ settlement chunks —
  distant chunks are non-resident (on disk). Overlapping camera/settlement footprints counted once
  (explicit story edge case).
- Transparent round-trip: a chunk written, evicted to a region file, then re-approached — `get_cell`
  returns the written value byte-identical; the accessor signature (`get`/`set` by `Vector3i`,
  `cell_changed`, `raycast_cells`) is unchanged before/after residency is introduced.
- Header I/O happens exactly once per region: a region touched repeatedly over many ticks shows
  synchronous header (offset-table) reads counted exactly 1 — never per-tick.
- Boot allocates only the initial residency set, not a full-world allocation (grep/assert: no
  full-world `PackedByteArray`-class allocation at boot — this is the story's own Forbidden clause).

**Edge cases to cover**:
- A world exactly one region in size (degenerate case — is there still a meaningful non-resident
  set, or does the whole world load resident?).
- A cell at a region boundary (page-in triggered exactly at the boundary, not one cell early/late).
- Zero prior mutations in a region — no region file is ever created on disk for it (per the spike's
  documented format: "a region that never has a dirty chunk never gets a file on disk at all" —
  worth asserting in production too, since it's a direct correctness/footprint claim).

**Estimated test count**: ~5-6

---

### vox-011 — Async region I/O + terrain-gen on a capped WorkerThreadPool — Integration
**Test file path**: `neues-spiel/tests/integration/voxel_world/async_region_io_test.gd`
(or a documented playtest, per the story's own declared alternate)

**What to test** (from story AC-1/2/3 / `TR-voxel-world-053/026`):
- **No sync I/O/gen in the frame path** (the sprint's named residency invariant): grep the
  residency source for synchronous region read/flush/terrain-gen calls reachable from the
  per-frame update path — zero matches outside the one sanctioned exception (per-region header
  I/O, vox-010 AC-3).
- **Cap-miss stays queued, never falls back to sync** (the sprint's named residency invariant): with
  the pool saturated at `MAX_CONCURRENT_ASYNC_TASKS`, an additional chunk needed stays queued and is
  dispatched on a later frame — no synchronous fallback occurs, no frame-time I/O spike. Edge case:
  many chunks needed in one frame (mass approach) — ALL beyond the cap stay queued, none silently
  falls back.
- **Mutex-guarded results, not `wait_for_task_completion`'s return** (the sprint's named
  async-torn-read condition): a completed background load's result is consumed from a
  mutex-guarded structure; assert (or grep) that no call site treats
  `WorkerThreadPool.wait_for_task_completion()`'s return value as loaded data — the spike's own
  documented bug (`typeof(ret) == TYPE_INT`, an Error code, not the Callable's return).
- **Main-thread-only integration of committed state** (no torn reads): a background task's result
  is only merged into the authoritative resident-set structure on the main thread; construct a test
  double that would reveal a race if the merge happened off-thread.

**Edge cases to cover**:
- A dispatch failure (pool at capacity) followed immediately by the same chunk becoming needed
  again next frame — must not double-dispatch or leak a task slot.
- `WorkerThreadPool`/`FileAccess` API shapes cross-referenced against `docs/engine-reference/godot/`
  before the test assumes a signature (HIGH engine-risk, post-cutoff APIs per the story's own
  Engine Notes) — do not assume 4.3-era signatures.

**Estimated test count**: ~5-6

### building-019 — Tool state machine (Idle / ToolArmed / Dragging / Suspended) — Logic
**Test file path**: `neues-spiel/tests/unit/building_system/tool_state_machine_test.gd`

**What to test** (from story AC2/AC3/AC37/AC44 / `TR-building-system-042/067`):
- AC2: Tool A armed, Tool B selected → A deactivates, B arms; exactly one tool ever active
  (assert never two simultaneously, not just "eventually one").
- AC3: a tool armed, cancel fires (Esc/right-click) → state returns to Idle, ghost-hide signal
  fires.
- AC37: Suspended entered mid-drag → drag aborts, no commit, no partial blueprint (now testable
  because cam-007's Suspended state landed in S4).
- AC44: a different tool selected mid-drag → drag aborts, no commit (same abort contract as AC37,
  different trigger).
- Post-abort, the SM lands in a clean armed/idle state, never stuck in Dragging (explicit story
  edge case for both AC37 and AC44).

**Edge cases to cover**:
- Cancel fired while already Idle (no-op, no error).
- Suspended entered while already Idle (no drag to abort — no error, no spurious signal).
- Rapid tool-A→tool-B→tool-A reselection does not leave a stale "previous tool" reference armed.

**Estimated test count**: ~6-7

### building-020 — DDA placement pick + surface-aware targeting — Logic
**Test file path**: `neues-spiel/tests/unit/building_system/dda_placement_pick_test.gd`

**What to test** (from story AC8 + surface-aware/zero-physics/highlight ACs / `TR-building-system-002/043/092`):
- AC8: a drag started on a block at height y > 0 keeps all preview/committed cells on that block's
  plane, never the ground plane — including dragging off the block's edge (locked plane holds).
- Surface-aware attach/replace: a picked block resolves to the adjacent face cell (attach) or the
  picked cell itself (replace), per tool mode; a pick on terrain top attaches to its face.
- **Zero physics in the pick path** (BLOCKING grep, per story + control-manifest): `rg --glob
  "*.gd" "intersect_ray|PhysicsDirectSpaceState3D|RayCast3D" src/building_system/` → zero matches.
- Pick never mutates voxel state (read-only) — assert no `set_cell`/write call anywhere in the
  pick path (this story's own explicit non-goal, since building-021's commit pipeline is Nice/not
  committed this sprint — the pick MUST stay side-effect-free until 021 lands).

**Edge cases to cover**:
- A ray that misses all geometry (no valid pick) — no crash, highlight clears.
- Ghost-anchored pick predicate boundary: a Planned blueprint cell picks as solid; a dig-order/water
  cell does not (per ADR-0014 §4's `extra_solid` overlay — coordinate with Voxel World's existing
  contract, do not add a second pick path here).

**Estimated test count**: ~6-7 (plus the zero-physics grep as a companion check)

**Secondary Visual/Feel facet (highlight)**: the picked-block highlight itself is not headlessly
verifiable (visual overlay). See Manual QA Checklist.

### villager-ai-003 — Body-column occupancy / clearance — Logic
**Test file path**: `neues-spiel/tests/unit/villager_ai/body_column_test.gd`

**What to test** (from story ACs / `TR-villager-ai-behavior-098`):
- `body_column(cell)` returns the deterministic 3-cell vertical span (feet + body + buffer headroom
  cell) derived purely from `current_cell` — same input always produces the same output
  (determinism, explicit story edge case).
- **Feet-only insufficiency** (the story's own named defect class): a feet cell that is standable
  but whose body cell is blocked by a low ceiling — the body-column check reports the villager's
  space as obstructed, where a feet-only check would incorrectly pass. This is the primary defect
  the story exists to prevent; test it explicitly, not just the happy path.
- The clearance constant is read from Story 002's shared `villager_clearance`, never a second copy
  (grep or fixture-driven assertion, same discipline villager-ai-002 established in Sprint 4).
- Purity: no mutation, no internal cache, no read of `_visual_position` or interpolation progress
  (grep-verifiable per the story's Forbidden clause).

**Edge cases to cover**:
- A low ceiling formed by Built blocks (not just terrain) still fails clearance — mirrors
  villager-ai-002's Sprint 4 edge case, now at the column level instead of the single-cell level.
- A Planned blueprint cell within the column (not just at the feet cell) still reads as
  non-solid/passable per the Building Core Rule 14b contract already established.

**Estimated test count**: ~5-6

### vox-012 — Time-based per-frame page-in / eviction budget (Should) — Integration
**Test file path**: `neues-spiel/tests/integration/voxel_world/time_based_streaming_budget_test.gd`
(or a documented playtest, per the story's own declared alternate)

**What to test** (from story AC-1/2 / `TR-voxel-world-053`):
- **Time-based, not count-based** (the sprint's named residency invariant): with many ready
  page-in results queued (simulated mass approach) and `page_budget_ms = 4.0`, integration stops
  when the 4.0 ms budget is reached, not at a fixed item count — remainder stays queued.
- A single item that alone exceeds the budget is still integrated (progress guaranteed), but the
  loop then stops for that frame — no further items integrated past it (explicit story edge case).
- Per-item re-check bounds bursts: total integration time per frame stays bounded near
  `page_budget_ms` even for a large burst of ready items; excess defers to later frames.
- Page-in and eviction budgets are tracked independently (`page_budget_ms` vs `evict_budget_ms`) —
  a page-in-heavy frame does not starve eviction's own separate budget or vice versa.

**Edge cases to cover**:
- Zero ready items in a frame (budget check is a no-op, no error).
- Exactly one item whose cost lands exactly at the budget boundary (off-by-one on the "stop"
  condition).

**Estimated test count**: ~4-5

### villager-ai-004 — Deterministic position model & movement interpolation (Should) — Logic
**Test file path**: `neues-spiel/tests/unit/villager_ai/deterministic_position_test.gd`

**What to test** (from story ACs / `TR-villager-ai-behavior-029/046/042/048/073/093`):
- `get_current_cell()` returns `from_cell` for a mid-transit villager (progress strictly between 0
  and 1) — never `to_cell`, never an interpolation-derived value. Test progress exactly 0 and
  exactly 1 as explicit boundary cases (does 1 correctly read as `to_cell`, i.e. arrived?).
- `current_cell` updates to `to_cell` in a single atomic assignment at the tick boundary where
  arrival is credited — no mid-interpolation flip observable from any intermediate progress sample.
- AC13: the first work-progress increment after arrival credits at the NEXT tick boundary, never
  partially — test at least one 1-cell adjacent-step Traveling→Working transition explicitly (the
  story's own named edge case, not just a multi-cell path).
- AC20 (property-based): given ≥5 injected `game_delta` samples (including one warped value),
  per-step displacement never exceeds `move_speed × game_delta` for any sample — assert directly
  against the movement-update function, no real engine frames.
- AC21: under pause, position is unchanged as real time passes; under 2x warp, wall-clock travel
  halves while game-time cost stays constant; `_visual_position` freezes during pause (advances on
  `game_delta`, never raw `_delta`).

**Edge cases to cover**:
- `physics_interpolation_mode == OFF` explicitly set on the villager visual node (grep/assert —
  defends against a project-wide interpolation flip causing double interpolation).
- Grep for any `_visual_position` read outside movement/rendering code, and for raw `_delta`
  integrated into `_intra_tick_progress` — both forbidden per the story's own Control Manifest
  Rules.

**Estimated test count**: ~7-8

### presentation-002 — Loop-payoff communication scaffolding (Should, CD-protected) — Integration
**Test file path**: `neues-spiel/tests/integration/presentation_experience/loop_payoff_surface_test.gd`

**What to test** (from story AC-1/2/3/4, milestone-01 exit criterion #10 scaffolding half):
- AC-1: the module wires via `setup()` with mock deps, instantiates headless (no Autoload, no
  file I/O), and the payoff signal surface is present and connectable.
- AC-2: a mock Feature-layer consumer binds to the surface and a stub emits a payoff signal — the
  consumer receives it; the surface signature does not need to change to accommodate the consumer.
  Edge case: a second consumer binds to the same signal without conflict.
- AC-3: a payoff signal keyed by (type, subject), re-emitted with the same key, is
  presentation-idempotent (refresh-in-place) — no duplicate-state error.
- AC-4: grep/review of the story diff confirms no payoff *mechanic* and no new simulation is
  introduced — this is the scaffolding-only boundary the CD sign-off (see Manual QA Checklist)
  also independently verifies.

**Edge cases to cover**:
- A consumer that binds AFTER a signal has already been emitted once (does the surface need
  replay semantics, or is "future emits only" the intended contract? — clarify with
  game-designer/CD if ambiguous; do not assume replay is required without confirming).

**Estimated test count**: ~5-6

## Smoke Test Scope

**Baseline**: 421 passing tests (311→421 across Sprint 4, per `sprint-04.md`'s own actuals — zero
red at close).

**What Sprint 5 adds**: up to 8 new test files (5 committed Must + 3 Should), summing to roughly
**~27-32 tests from the 5 committed Must stories** (vox-010 ~5-6, vox-011 ~5-6, building-019 ~6-7,
building-020 ~6-7, villager-ai-003 ~5-6) plus **~16-19 more if all 3 Should stories land** (vox-012
~4-5, villager-ai-004 ~7-8, presentation-002 ~5-6). Target regression count at sprint close:
**~448-453 passing** (committed-only) or **~464-472** (if all three Should land) — zero failures,
zero errors, zero skipped.

1. **Full regression suite runs green**: all 421 existing tests PLUS every new Sprint-5 test file
   above via `tests\run-tests.cmd` — 421 is a floor, not a ceiling.

2. **Residency-invariant smoke items — named per the sprint's own risk concentration (ADR-0015
   cluster), not folded into a generic line:**
   - **No-sync-in-frame-path grep**: grep the residency streaming source for synchronous region
     read/flush/terrain-gen calls reachable from the per-frame update path — **zero matches**
     outside the one sanctioned exception (per-region header I/O, vox-010 AC-3). This is the
     spike's single most load-bearing finding (lever 1 of round 3) — it gets its own named smoke
     gate, not a bullet buried in a general regression line.
   - **Async-torn-read condition — mutex-guarded results, not `wait_for_task_completion` return**:
     grep for any call site that treats `WorkerThreadPool.wait_for_task_completion()`'s return
     value as loaded/generated data (as opposed to an error/status check) — **zero matches**. This
     is the spike's own documented implementation bug (an Error code mistaken for a Callable's
     return); re-checking it at smoke time, not just at story-completion time, guards against a
     regression introduced by a later Sprint-5 story touching the same file.
   - **Cap-miss-stays-queued, no synchronous fallback**: confirm (via the integration test's own
     assertion, re-run at hand-off) that a chunk failing to dispatch (pool at capacity) stays
     queued rather than falling back to a synchronous read/regen — the exact failure mode the
     spike's round-2 10.1-second-tick bug demonstrated before the round-3 fix.
   - **Time-based budget, not fixed count** (vox-012, if landed): grep for any reintroduction of a
     fixed chunks-per-frame streaming count (ADR-0014's `stream_chunk_budget` style) in the
     residency loop — zero matches; the config knobs must be `page_budget_ms`/`evict_budget_ms`
     (time-based) per the story's own Forbidden clause.
   - **Header I/O once per region**: re-confirm via the vox-010 test's own assertion that repeated
     ticks touching the same region do not re-read/re-create its header.
   - **Full-world allocation absent at boot**: grep/assert no full-world-sized `PackedByteArray`-
     class allocation exists at boot (the story's own Forbidden clause) — this is the residency
     tier's core promise (footprint-bounded memory) and deserves its own explicit re-check, not an
     assumption from the AC passing once.
   - **Scope reminder (see Classification Note #3)**: these smoke items certify what 010/011/012
     actually implement. They do **not** certify the in-flight-write race (Story 013) or
     far-world load-before-write (Story 014) — both out of scope this sprint. Do not read a green
     smoke pass here as "the full ADR-0015 invariant set is closed."

3. **Building System grep-guard families — inherited from the established project conventions**
   (Voxel World's ADR-0004/0014 picking guardrails, now extended to Building System's first two
   stories):
   - Zero physics API calls in Building System's pick path: `rg --glob "*.gd"
     "intersect_ray|PhysicsDirectSpaceState3D" src/building_system/` — zero matches (control-manifest
     line 89, this sprint's first exercise of that rule for Building System).

   - No `MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED` during placement drags, and no `mouse_filter` geometry restructuring

5. **CW-winding / culling regression (carried forward, unaffected by this sprint's stories but part

   API shapes used by vox-011 (and the DDA `raycast_cells()` signature building-020 depends on)
   are confirmed against `docs/engine-reference/godot/` before trusting any test that assumes
   their behavior — both vox-011 and building-020 are flagged HIGH risk in their own story headers.

7. **Performance is within budget** — with the caveat that this sprint's residency work is
   **data-layer only, no rendering/meshing hookup** (per the spike README's own scope note: "Data
   layer only: no rendering/meshing... unexercised here" — vox-015, which would make this
   measurable end-to-end, is Nice-to-have and not committed). So:
   - The time-based budget's own re-check discipline (vox-012, if landed) is verified by its
     integration test's timing assertions, not by an in-engine frame-time measurement — there is
     no rendered view-window yet to profile against.
   - Building's DDA hover-pick stays O(1) per the story's own Guardrail — verify via the unit
     test's own timing assertion if one exists, or note as a code-review spot-check (not a
     rendered-frame measurement, since Building doesn't render committed geometry changes this
     sprint either — no commit pipeline lands).
   - **No windowed/rendered perf check is warranted this sprint for the residency cluster** — flag
     this explicitly rather than silently skipping it, since it might otherwise look like an
     oversight. Re-evaluate once vox-015 (Nice, view-window streaming) lands and gives the
     residency tier something to profile against on-screen.

## Playtest Requirements

**No mandatory playtest sessions required for this sprint.** Every committed Logic/Integration
story's primary evidence path is an automated headless test.

- **vox-010, vox-011, and vox-012** each declare "integration test OR documented playtest" as
  their own alternate evidence path (same pattern as Sprints 2-4's precedent stories). If any
  team elects the playtest route, it must be written to
  `production/session-logs/playtest-sprint-5-[story-slug].md` and reviewed by qa-lead before the
  story is marked Complete.
- No end-to-end "place a wall and watch a villager react to it" playtest is warranted THIS sprint —
  Building System's commit pipeline (story-021) is Nice-to-have and not committed, so there is no
  functional placement loop yet to playtest; building-020's pick is explicitly read-only. This
  mirrors the sprint's own Out-of-Scope note that the integrated E2E LOOP (milestone criterion #8)
  targets Sprint 6.

If no stories require playtest validation beyond the above: this statement stands as the sprint's
playtest posture. Re-evaluate once Sprint 6 lands the Building commit pipeline and Villager
movement/FSM stories, giving a real playtester an end-to-end loop to react to for the first time.

## Definition of Done — This Sprint

A story is DONE when ALL of the following are true:

- [ ] All acceptance criteria verified — via a passing automated test result. By declared Type
      (see Classification Note #1 for the building-020 correction): **4 Integration** stories —
      vox-010, vox-011, vox-012, presentation-002; **4 Logic** stories — building-019,
      building-020, villager-ai-003, villager-ai-004 — OR documented manual evidence for the
      declared alternate-path stories (vox-010/011/012's playtest alternate, if elected)
- [ ] Test file exists at the canonical `neues-spiel/tests/[unit|integration]/[system]/...` path
      listed in this plan's Test Summary table for all 8 stories
- [ ] building-020's picked-block highlight has screenshot evidence at
      `production/qa/evidence/dda-placement-pick-highlight-evidence.md` with qa-lead sign-off
      (ADVISORY — does not block building-020 Done on its own)
- [ ] presentation-002 (if landed) has BOTH its automated integration test passing AND a CD
      sign-off note on scaffolding-only scope in `production/qa/evidence/` (see Classification
      Note #2 — the sprint file's DoD prose undersells this to "interaction/smoke evidence" alone;
      this plan requires both)
- [ ] Full regression suite passes (`/smoke-check sprint`) — 421-test baseline plus every new
      Sprint-5 test file, zero failures/errors/skips, **plus the named residency-invariant and
      Building grep-guard smoke items (Smoke Test Scope items 2-4) explicitly re-checked at
      hand-off, not assumed still-true from story-completion time**
- [ ] The residency-invariant smoke pass is understood to cover ONLY stories 010/011/012 — it does
      NOT certify Story 013 (in-flight-write cache) or Story 014 (load-before-write far-world),
      neither of which is committed this sprint (Classification Note #3)
- [ ] No regressions introduced — the carried-forward project-wide forbidden patterns
      (`SceneTree.paused`, `Engine.time_scale`, zero-physics picking, `CULL_DISABLED`) remain
      absent; villager-ai-003 (+004 if landed) extends the NavigationServer3D-family guardrail
      Sprint 4 established; building-019/020 introduce the FIRST exercise of the zero-physics
      Building System guardrail
- [ ] No open S1 or S2 bugs in delivered stories
- [ ] Code reviewed (via `/code-review` or documented peer review)
- [ ] Story file updated to `Status: Complete` (via `/story-done`)

This plan corrects `sprint-05.md`'s own Definition of Done in two places (see Classification Notes
1 and 2): building-020 is a Logic story requiring a unit test, not an Integration story; and
presentation-002 requires a BLOCKING automated integration test in addition to (not instead of) its
CD sign-off. All 8 stories carry BLOCKING automated-test evidence — the highest blocking ratio of
any sprint so far (8 of 8, vs. Sprint 4's 7 of 8) — because this sprint has no primary Visual/Feel
or UI story; the one Visual/Feel facet present (building-020's highlight) is a secondary,
ADVISORY-only component of an otherwise Logic story.
